analysis.title: GS materials Oct 28 results: SSAB/EQNR/FORTUM/ELE/ILU, FCX trims, EGO incoming, FM a big ask. TECK's hurdle, SSAB. GLEN hurdle, LME feedback
key_insights: Desk views the bar as low for miners. Results so far have been broadly fine (ANTO and NHY the exceptions). FM, TECK, GLEN and EGO are expected to 'travel fine' into their prints.
BHP moved sharply on 10/27, attributed to transition flow in Australia. The move did not extend overnight. BHP is described as a consensus short.

Copper is the key ask. The action is in the physical market while the financial market is quiet on tariff uncertainty. Backwardation started to extend, the China physical premium continued to expand, and mine supply continued to miss (FCX). If tariffs come, the desk argues stocks run out.

Met coal rose in the night session. Market chatter says China-Mongolia cross-border coal clearance will stay constrained below 1,000 trucks per day because of quota exhaustion and negotiation friction.
AAL.LN update: the EC review of the nickel sale was extended to Dec 21.
RIO: iron ore may be up but sits at $90. A new incentive plan could raise pay by 56%, which the desk describes as incentive based. US pay is already considerably higher.
Uranium names trade well off their lows. Kazakhstan's president said the country should create a state strategic uranium reserve covering domestic plant needs for 100 years.

Equinor starts -1%: EBIT $12.3bn vs consensus $12.2bn, trading (MMP) beat, misses in E&P US and international, CFFO ex-WC $8.1bn in line, production guide nudged up, buyback, dividend and capex unchanged. Desk expects EQNR to underperform while the sector bounces.

SSAB: EBITDA SEK 3.26bn vs consensus SEK 3.06bn, EPS SEK 1.56 vs consensus 1.63. Capex guide trimmed to SEK 11.2bn from 13.5bn on revised payment timing. Q4 pricing guide looks underwhelming against peers, with plate spread compression in Europe and Americas.

Endesa starts -2-3%: numbers in line (9M EBITDA EUR 4.58bn vs consensus 4.59bn, NI EUR 1.96bn vs 1.95bn). Buyback pace slowed. The desk thinks hedge funds waited for a beat and raise and that this will be the Q4 funding short.
Fortum: EBIT EUR 102m vs consensus EUR 105m. Generation beat, consumer solutions dragged. Nothing new on datacentres, which could fade without an update on the call.
REDIA (Redeia) was in line with consensus at EBITDA and net income. Full-year guidance reaffirmed.

First Quantum (FM): stock cheap at under 4x at spot. Cobre Panama restart is a 6-9 month process, stockpiles last until March 2027, and consensus has 2027 at 115kt. The board visited Argentina (Taca Taca 275-300kt, $6.8bn, first production 2035) and La Granja Peru is longer dated ($7.2bn, 200kt).

Equinox Gold (EGO): stock +6% on 10/27 but down c.35% since summer (-13% vs GDX). Desk expects cost creep, lower production and capex creep at Skouries and McIvenna Bay. Short interest is c.5m shares (5% of float), down 25% from highs but high vs peers. Focus is an FCF inflection after the CEO change.
Teck: bar is not high. Zinc, with the smelter printing money in the seasonally best quarter, is where a beat would come from. QB copper needs a push. Desk is happy to run pretty long into the print.

FCX: 2026/27 production guidance cut by about 100m lbs a year. Grasberg ramp is on track. 2027 capex rises $400m (+8%) to $5.2bn on inflation, equipment and project spend. Bagdad FID update expected ahead of year end.
Nucor: market is watching prices closely and is scared of being run over by the buyback.

Glencore reports Thursday. Consensus looks in line. Key items are Katanga (consensus 55kt) and zinc (consensus 175kt). Stock is 540p vs 630p earlier. It is a consensus long. Kazzinc close expected by year end, and Argentina approved the $6.4bn Agua Rica project.

LME conference feedback: scarce copper supply, declining grades, rising capital intensity, permitting complexity and geopolitical fragmentation. Governments are more active through tariffs, stockpiling and financing. Companies are focused on capital discipline and asset sales.

China midday wrap: rebound led by Physical AI and robotics. Baijiu fell on an earnings miss by the industry leader. Unitree rebounded nearly 70% from its Oct 15 low of 404 Rmb and reports Q3 after the close. Financials and SOEs under pressure.
